The test image shows an opened soybean pod with two seeds (yellowish-green and green) and prominent **white cottony/fluffy material** lining the inside of the pod and along the seams. The pod wall has brown discoloration. This white mycelial growth inside the pod is a strong indicator.

Top candidates: **White_Mold**, Phomopsis, Purple_Seed_Stain

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with White_Mold.
This White Mold reference shows stem bleaching with black sclerotia. The test image shows pod interior with white cottony growth. Let me check another White Mold image.
This White Mold reference shows white cottony mycelium, which matches the test image. Now let me check Phomopsis (pod/seed infection candidate).
Very interesting! Phomopsis reference shows an opened pod with white cottony material around a damaged seed. Let me check another Phomopsis image.
Phomopsis shows shrunken/rotted seeds. Test image seeds look fuller. Let me check Purple_Seed_Stain and a few more candidates.
Not Purple_Seed_Stain - no purple staining in test. Let me check Anthracnose (pod infection candidate).
Not matching. Let me check Downy_mildew, Bacterial_Blight, Frogeye_leaf_spot, Septoria, Sudden_death_syndrome to cover required 16 classes.
Need 4 more classes to cover. Let me check Soybean_rust, Cercospora, Powdery_Mildew, and Charcoal_Rot.

All 16 views complete. Summary of findings:

- **Test image**: Opened soybean pod with two full-looking seeds (yellow-green, green) and prominent **white cottony/fluffy mycelial growth** lining the pod interior and seams. Pod wall has some browning.
- **White_Mold refs**: Soybean_Dise_415 shows white cottony mycelium matching the test image texture. Other refs show stem/whole-plant symptoms.
- **Phomopsis ref (Dise_14)**: Also shows opened pod with white material, but the seed inside is heavily shrunken/rotted — unlike the test image where seeds look fuller.
- All other classes (leaf spots, stem rots, whole-plant wilts) clearly don't match the pod-interior white growth presentation.

The white cottony mycelium inside the pod is the defining feature. White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum) is the primary soybean disease producing this abundant white mycelial growth inside pods, and the texture/appearance in the test image aligns with the White_Mold references.
